20. A student suggests a trick for gaining profit in a business. He suggests buying oranges from the mountain and selling
them to Terai at the cost price. If a beam balance is used during this transaction, explain, based on scientific fact, whether his
trick goes wrong or right.
Ans:- It fails. A beam balance compares masses, not weights; it cancels the local value of g. If you get 1 kg of oranges in the
mountain, you still have 1 kg when you sell in Terai. Although local weight (force) changes slightly with g, the beam balance
shows equal masses regardless of location, so no profit. (If one used a spring scale instead, readings change with local g, so
that could cause apparent differences.)
21. The acceleration of an object moving on the earth is inversely proportional to the mass of the object but for an object
falling towards the surface of the earth, the acceleration does not depend on the mass of the object, why?
Ans:- In general, acceleration is inversely proportional to mass because the same force causes less acceleration in heavier
objects.But in free fall, the gravitational force is mg, which increases with mass, so when we calculate acceleration: a=F/m
=mg/m= gThe mass cancels out.
So, all objects fall with the same acceleration because gravity increases the force and inertia equally, making acceleration
independent of mass. 22. The acceleration due to gravity of the Mars is 3.75 m/s2. How much mass can a weight-lifter lift on Mars who can lift
100 kg mass on the Earth. (Ans: 261.33 kg)
Ans:- The weight-lifter can lift the same maximum force on any planet.He lifts 100 kg on earth so F=mg=100 * 9.8 =
980NThis is the maximum force he can exert.So on Mars, let the liftable mass be m so
F=mg or, 980= m*3.75 or, m=261.3 kg So he can lift about 261kg on Mars.
